title: Business Plan
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Pre-Technical Studies; not yet checked by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher; safety lines marked SAFETY in the library to confirm first; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The learner explains why a business plan matters (guides the owner, shows if the idea can work, helps get loans and partners, sets goals) and describes its components (executive summary, business description, market and competitors, marketing plan, operations, management, financial plan).
contexts: a youth applying for a loan
a school club starting a business
a tailor planning a second shop

board.do: Write the components on cards in a pile.
Wait for the learner to say costs, sales and profit.

listen_for: It is a waste of time
misconceptions.repair: Compare two traders: one who planned costs and market and one who did not; list what went wrong for the second.

listen_for: Nothing; a good product sells itself
misconceptions.ask: A business plan describes the product. What else must it show?
misconceptions.repair: Read a short plan with no market section; ask who will buy and who else sells the same thing.

misconceptions.ask: Which part shows costs and income?
misconceptions.repair: Point to the financial plan in a template: start-up costs, expected sales, costs and profit.

listen_for: Keep it as it is; plans are written once
misconceptions.ask: A business plan was written a year ago and prices have changed. What should the owner do?
misconceptions.repair: Change one price in a plan and see how the profit changes; plan a review each term.

checks.question: Give one reason for a business plan.
checks.answer: It guides the owner (helps get a loan)

checks.question: Name a component of a business plan.

skills.key_step: The learner fills in a business plan template for a small project: description, market and competitors, operations, start-up capital, projected sales, costs and profit, and the executive summary written last; the filled template is marked with the rubric.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the parts of a business plan.
floor.question: Name one part of a business plan.

representations: a projected profit row: sales - costs
steps: Cost the start-up and project sales, costs and profit.
contexts: a juice stall at a school fair

board.do: Wait for the learner to say 8,000.
Fill in the rest of the financial part.

misconceptions.ask: A learner plans a juice stall. Which costs go into the start-up capital?
misconceptions.repair: List everything needed before the first sale; sort it into equipment, permits and stock.

misconceptions.ask: Projected sales 30,000 shillings a month, projected costs 22,000. What is the projected profit?
misconceptions.repair: Write profit = sales - costs in the template row itself; fill it in for three businesses.

misconceptions.ask: When is the executive summary of a business plan written?
misconceptions.repair: Try to summarise an empty plan; then fill the parts and summarise. Only the second works.

listen_for: Nothing; competitors need not be in a plan
misconceptions.ask: A learner writes "no competitors" for a mandazi stall beside two kiosks that sell mandazi. What is wrong?
misconceptions.repair: Walk the market (or a map) and list every seller of the same goods; write one way the new stall will be different.

checks.question: When is the executive summary written?
